name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
description: NIST CSF 2.0 baseline overlay — always active for all agents. The AKSIs are organized by CSF functions, making this the most direct and natural mapping. Provides CSF-specific evidence packaging for organizations demonstrating framework alignment.

Network and environment monitored for cybersecurity events (DE.CM-01)
Computing hardware and software monitored for configuration changes (DE.CM-09)
Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into continuous compliance monitoring (DE.AE-07)
The estimated impact and scope of compliance deviations are understood and communicated (DE.AE-04)
Anomalous activity is detected in a timely manner for compliance posture assessment (DE.AE-02)
Computing platforms monitored for integrity (DE.CM-09)
Event data integrity verified
Incident response plan executed during or after an incident (RS.MA-01)
Incident reports provided to designated stakeholders (RS.MA-02)
Response activities coordinated with internal and external stakeholders (RS.CO-02)
Information shared with designated authorities as required (RS.CO-03)
Investigation of incidents conducted to support response (RS.AN-03)

Recovery planning and processes improved incorporating lessons learned (RC.IM-01)
Recovery strategies updated based on experience (RC.IM-02)

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: NIST CSF is voluntary. No formal certification or assessment requirement. Organizations self-assess alignment using CSF Profiles (Current and Target). Third-party assessments optional. The Framework is used to communicate risk posture, not for pass/fail compliance.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: No mandatory reporting entity. CSF Profiles used internally and shared with stakeholders as needed.

human_oversight_mandates.description: NIST CSF 2.0 does not mandate specific human oversight configurations. Individual subcategories (GV.OV, RS.CO) reference oversight and communication but do not prescribe specific human-in-the-loop requirements.

notes: NIST CSF 2.0 is the most widely adopted cybersecurity framework globally. The AKSIs are explicitly organized by CSF 2.0 functions (GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, RECOVER), making this the cleanest and most natural mapping. NIST CSF evidence is about demonstrating alignment, not pass/fail compliance. This overlay is always active as a baseline — it does not set strict thresholds or additional evidence requirements beyond what baseline controls already provide.
